# Stacks and CI

Version control is the root's alone, through `holyagent vcs` (the CLI path is in the `assignments` skill). The target repository's conventions, found in CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and its branch and PR history, come first; `vcs detect` reports its remote, base branch, account owner and CI.

## Commands

- `vcs branch <name> [--from <ref>]`
- `vcs commit -m <headline> [-m <body>] -- <paths…>` stages those paths and the Intent's state folder, and commits as the account owner. Name the paths of the accepted Assignments only, so code and unrelated work stay apart.
- `vcs push [branches…]`
- `vcs pr --base <b> --title <t> [--body-file f] [--update n]` opens a PR ready for review, or updates one.
- `vcs ci <n|sha> [--watch]`

## Stack plan

- One branch and one PR per reviewable change. Independent changes branch from the base; stack on another PR only when it needs that PR's code or touches the same lines, since each stacked link is a merge to redo when a lower PR changes. Parallel writers on the same files cost conflicts and a second review.
- The first PR of a stack targets the base, each later one its immediate predecessor; verify real PR bases rather than inferring them from names. No aggregate PR.
- A writer starts from the current stack head. When lower PRs change, merge forward with merge commits, once per batch of repairs, and push the affected branches together. Published history is never rewritten; a force-push needs the user's approval. A conflicted generated file is rebuilt with the project's build task, and a conflicted state record keeps the side the later CLI write produced.
- Finish and review a PR before stacking the next on it. Each PR's head passes the gates alone, and accepted work is pushed so nothing stays only local.
- Branch names follow the repository's convention. Without one and when the version workflow fits, `release/<version>/<type>/<change>` for release work and `exp/<experiment>/<type>/<change>` for experiments, keeping the project's real version string. A name grants no merge, release or deploy authority.

## CI

Watch with Monitor running `holyagent vcs ci <n> --watch`, which prints a line per change of state and ends when every check settles. Read it as follows.

- Aggregate Failed, then Unknown, then Pending, then Passed. Missing or unreadable data is Unknown; in-progress checks are Pending; skipped and neutral results satisfy branch protection but are not validation and never make Passed alone.
- A snapshot belongs to one head SHA. After a push or merge-forward, watch the new SHA; an old approval or merge-state read is history.
- Diagnose a failure from the current attempt's logs. After the same gate fails twice, reproduce it with the repository's own script before pushing again. Call a failure environmental only after reading its message and reproducing it on the base.
- A repository with no CI workflow has the gate Unknown (none configured); finish on local gates and independent review. A watch that ends without a result leaves the gate Unknown.
- A PR is merge-ready when independent review of that head left no open blockers and its CI is Passed; merging still needs the user's approval. Report an unresolved review thread or a merge state other than clean beside the checks.
- Treat review-bot findings as claims to verify, fix the real ones with review, and answer the rest on the thread when replying is authorized.

## PR text

PR text says what changed and why, how it was checked and what remains, concisely, in the target repository's language and format. The commit rule in the root prompt applies to it: the account owner's voice, no attribution, no mention of agents, Claude, Assignments, reviews or "the user".
